subject: mathematics
question_text: Determine whether f(x) = x((eˣ − 1)/(eˣ + 1)) is even or odd.

mark_split.label: Compare with f(x) and name the parity

recall_prompt: Say how you would decide this — what you write for f(−x), and what you compare it with.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write f(−x) and clear e⁻ˣ
steps.margin_note: One mark for f(−x) with e⁻ˣ cleared. State the domain first: eˣ + 1 > 0 for every x, so the domain is R and −x is always in it.
steps.memory_tip: Replace e⁻ˣ by 1/eˣ, then multiply the top and the bottom of the fraction by eˣ. Both negative powers go in one move.
lines: eˣ + 1 > 0 for every x, so the domain is R,
and −x is in the domain whenever x is.
e⁻ˣ = 1/eˣ. Multiply top and bottom by eˣ:

recall.must_convey: That f(−x) = −x(e⁻ˣ − 1)/(e⁻ˣ + 1), and that multiplying the top and bottom by eˣ turns it into −x(1 − eˣ)/(1 + eˣ).

steps.why: Parity is decided by comparing f(−x) with f(x), so f(−x) has to be written in the same letters as f(x). The negative powers e⁻ˣ are what block the comparison, and clearing them is the whole of this step.
common_mistakes: Losing the outside factor −x and writing f(−x) with a leading +x.
Treating e⁻ˣ as −eˣ, which is not the same thing.
Multiplying only the numerator by eˣ and leaving the denominator unchanged.

steps.label: Compare and name the parity
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the comparison and the word. Show the two minus signs cancelling, write f(−x) = f(x), then name the function even.
steps.memory_tip: Two sign changes make no sign change: the outside −x and the flipped fraction 1 − eˣ cancel each other, so the function is even.

lines.text: ∴ f is an even function on R.

recall.must_convey: That 1 − eˣ = −(eˣ − 1), so the two minus signs cancel and f(−x) = f(x), which makes f an even function.

steps.why: There are two sign changes here, not one: the outside factor becomes −x and the fraction flips to −(eˣ − 1)/(eˣ + 1). Two sign changes leave the value unchanged, so the function is even. A numerical check agrees — f(0.6) and f(−0.6) are both 0.1748, and f(1.7) and f(−1.7) are both 1.1748.
common_mistakes: Counting only one sign change and calling the function odd.
Writing 1 − eˣ = eˣ − 1, which loses a minus sign.
Naming a parity without ever writing the line f(−x) = f(x).
